correctness.rationale: For all n>=3, solve the two finite-neighborhood equations over F3. Their elimination is the recurrence a_(i-2)+a_i+a_(i+2)=0. Nonzero horizontal differences give precisely 36 initial quadruples and a six-column period; the relation a_(i+3)=b_i exchanges rows. Periodic and twisted closure yield the entire displayed table and the six period-three patterns. The executable supplied in artifacts/verify.py separately checks direct vertex labelings, an 81-state transfer, and explicit patterns, but the infinite claim follows from the recurrence, not those finite tests.

originality.rationale: The new result is all-coloring classification and sharp labelled counts on a pair of natural families. The full Minyard–Sepanski HTML and explicit existing theorems establish only existence for the relevant graph families; recent cubic total-domatic abstracts address different questions. Accessible published mathematical records do not imply the new census. The 2020 injective-coloring full text was inaccessible and remains an explicit priority risk; no assertion of exhaustive global originality is made.

value.rationale: For an infinite pair of naturally studied cubic families, the theorem identifies all 36 possible infinite-strip colorings, an exact period-six rigidity and period-three row-swap law, and a sharp 6-versus-36 labelled-count transition that reverses under a Möbius twist. It is a nontrivial configuration census refining known existence and total-domatic-number statements, with a direct enumerative interpretation as one or six unordered three-class total-domatic partitions.
